name: Episcopal City of Albi
description: Albi sits on the banks of the Tarn in south-west France, its skyline ruled by a vast fortress-like cathedral built of glowing red-orange brick in the late 13th century. Beside it stands the bishop's Palais de la Berbie, which looks out over the river. Around them, medieval streets and an old bridge survive largely as they were. The palace now houses the Toulouse-Lautrec museum.
